extracted.intended_audience: AQA GCSE English Language teachers/examiners (and students/reference for centre staff)
extracted.subtask_description: Mark scheme for AQA GCSE English Language Paper 1 (Explorations in creative reading and writing) giving assessment objectives, question-specific marking guidance and level descriptors for awarding marks.

rubrics_metrics.name: Level of response marking instructions
rubrics_metrics.description: Level of response mark schemes are broken down into four levels. There are two, four, five or six marks in each level; dependent upon question.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Step 1 Determine a level: start at the lowest level and climb until the descriptor matches the answer. Step 2 Determine a mark: once a level is assigned, decide the mark within that level; read back through the answer to clarify. To achieve full marks in a level, students should meet all skills descriptors in that level. Students at the bottom of a level will usually have met all descriptors of the previous level and at least one descriptor in the current level. An answer with nothing relevant scores 0.

rubrics_metrics.name: AO1: Identify and interpret information and ideas
rubrics_metrics.description: Identify and interpret explicit and implicit information and ideas; select and synthesise evidence from different texts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used to assess identification and selection of relevant information (e.g., Q1 'List four things...'). Responses must be true and drawn from the specified lines; paraphrase and quotation allowed; copying the whole passage verbatim does not evidence identification and should not be credited.

rubrics_metrics.name: AO2 (language): Explain, comment on and analyse language
rubrics_metrics.description: Explain, comment on and analyse how writers use language to achieve effects and influence readers, using relevant subject terminology to support views.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Question prompts may specify focus (e.g. words and phrases, language features and techniques, sentence forms). Level descriptors (Levels 1–4) judge depth: Level 4 = detailed, perceptive analysis (7–8 marks for an 8-mark question), selects judicious range of textual detail, sophisticated and accurate subject terminology; Level 3 = clear explanation; Level 2 = some understanding/comment; Level 1 = simple limited comment. Indicative content may include sentence length related to content, use of nouns/verbs, imagery such as simile, cumulative effect of chosen words and phrases. Exemplars demonstrate how to link textual detail to effect (e.g., analyse verbs, adjectives, similes).

rubrics_metrics.name: AO2 (structure): Explain, comment on and analyse structure
rubrics_metrics.description: Explain, comment on and analyse how writers use structural features to achieve effects and influence readers, using relevant subject terminology to support views.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Structural features include whole-text level (beginnings/endings/perspective shifts), paragraph level (topic change/cohesion) and sentence level where contributing to whole structure. Level descriptors (Levels 1–4) parallel language criteria: Level 4 = perceptive, detailed analysis (7–8 marks for an 8-mark question), selecting a judicious range, using sophisticated terminology; lower levels indicate progressively less detailed explanation. AO2 content may include overall journey structure (e.g., outside→inside), recurring motifs (weather), narrowing focus to individuals, and paragraphing.

rubrics_metrics.name: AO3: Compare writers' ideas and perspectives
rubrics_metrics.description: Compare writers’ ideas and perspectives, as well as how these are conveyed, across two or more texts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: AO3 is an assessment objective listed for Section A (reading). Although not used for every question on this paper, it defines the skillset expected when comparison across texts is required: identify and compare ideas and methods of conveyance.

rubrics_metrics.name: AO4: Evaluate texts critically and support with references
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluate texts critically and support this with appropriate textual references.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used for extended evaluative questions (e.g., Q4 'To what extent do you agree?'). Level descriptors for 20-mark Q4: Level 4 (16–20) = perceptive, detailed evaluation; evaluates effects on the reader, shows perceptive understanding of writer’s methods, selects judicious textual detail, develops convincing critical response. Level 3 (11–15) = clear relevant evaluation; Level 2 (6–10) = some evaluation; Level 1 (1–5) = simple limited evaluation; Level 0 = no relevant comments. AO4 content may include evaluating collective vs individual characterisation, interactions and use of language/structure/tone to create impressions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Q1 specific marking rules (listing facts from a specified passage)
rubrics_metrics.description: List four things from this part of the text about the weather in Cornwall. [4 marks] Give 1 mark for each point about the weather.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Responses must be true and drawn only from the specified lines; responses must relate to the weather. Students may quote or paraphrase. A paraphrased response covering more than one point should be credited for each point made, provided paraphrase demonstrates identification specific to the question focus (AO1). Responses that copy the whole section verbatim should not be credited. Indicative content lists example weather points (e.g., it was a cold day; the weather had changed overnight; there was a wind; there was mist on the hills; the air was clammy; the air was cold; it was raining) but is not exhaustive.

rubrics_metrics.name: Q2 marking (language question) — levels and expectations
rubrics_metrics.description: How does the writer use language here to describe the effects of the weather? [8 marks] You could include the writer’s choice of words and phrases, language features and techniques, sentence forms.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assesses AO2 language. Level 4 (7–8 marks) = detailed, perceptive analysis; analyses effects of writer’s choices, selects judicious range of textual detail, makes sophisticated and accurate use of subject terminology. Level 3 (5–6) = clear, relevant explanation with clear terminology; Level 2 (3–4) = some understanding/comment with some terminology; Level 1 (1–2) = simple limited comment selecting simple references. Level 0 = no comments. Indicative points: sentence length related to content, use of nouns/verbs to enhance description, imagery such as simile, cumulative effect of words and phrases. Example exemplar commentary is provided to illustrate standards at levels.

rubrics_metrics.name: Q3 marking (structure question) — levels and expectations
rubrics_metrics.description: How has the writer structured the text to interest you as a reader? [8 marks] You could write about what the writer focuses your attention on at the beginning, how and why the writer changes that focus, any other structural features.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assesses AO2 structure. Level 4 (7–8 marks) = perceptive, detailed analysis; analyses effects of structural choices, selects judicious examples, uses sophisticated terminology. Level 3 (5–6) = clear explanation; Level 2 (3–4) = some understanding/comment; Level 1 (1–2) = simple limited comment; Level 0 = no marks. Indicative content includes journey structure (general→specific; outside→inside), persistent weather motif, narrowing to individual characters, paragraphing and focus shifts. Exemplars illustrate how to connect structural features to reader effect.

rubrics_metrics.name: Q4 marking (evaluation of characters) — AO4 levels & indicative content
rubrics_metrics.description: To what extent do you agree? 'The writer brings the very different characters to life for the reader. It is as if you are inside the coach with them.' [20 marks]
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assesses AO4. Level 4 (16–20) demands perceptive, detailed evaluation: evaluate effects on reader, show perceptive understanding of writer’s methods, select judicious textual detail and develop convincing critical response. Lower levels denote progressively less detailed evaluation. Indicative content suggests considering passengers as a unified group vs individual characteristics, interactions and dynamics, and techniques (language, structure, tone) used to create impressions. Exemplars show how to evaluate irony, characterization, and behavioural detail to support judgments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Q5 task rubric: creative writing task requirements and assessment split
rubrics_metrics.description: Creative writing task: Write a description suggested by the picture OR write the opening part of a story about a place that is severely affected by the weather. Your entry will be judged by a panel of people of your own age. [40 marks: 24 marks for content and organisation and 16 marks for technical accuracy]
rubrics_metrics.guidance: AO5 assesses content and organisation (24 marks) and AO6 assesses technical accuracy (16 marks). Candidates should select and adapt tone, style and register for audience, organise information and ideas using structural and grammatical features to support coherence and cohesion, and use a range of vocabulary and sentence structures with accurate spelling and punctuation.

rubrics_metrics.name: AO5 Content and Organisation (creative writing) — levels and descriptors
rubrics_metrics.description: AO5: Communicate clearly, effectively and imaginatively, selecting and adapting tone, style and register; organise information and ideas using structural and grammatical features to support coherence and cohesion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Marking bands for 24-mark AO5: Level 4 (19–24) = Compelling, convincing. Upper Level 4 (22–24): register is convincing and compelling for audience; assuredly matched to purpose; extensive and ambitious vocabulary with sustained crafting of linguistic devices; varied and inventive structural features; compelling writing with complex ideas and fluently linked paragraphs and seamlessly integrated discourse markers. Lower Level 4 (19–21): convincingly matched register and purpose, extensive vocabulary, varied/effective structure. Level 3 (13–18) = Consistent, clear (upper/lower splits indicate degree of sophistication). Level 2 (7–12) = Some success (upper/lower splits indicate attempts to match register/purpose and organisation). Level 1 (1–6) = Simple, limited (occasional sense of audience/purpose, simple vocabulary, limited structure). Level 0 = No meaningful writing. Guidance emphasizes register, vocabulary choice, use of linguistic devices, paragraphing, discourse markers, and coherence.

rubrics_metrics.name: AO6 Technical Accuracy (creative writing) — levels and descriptors
rubrics_metrics.description: AO6: Use a range of vocabulary and sentence structures for clarity, purpose and effect, with accurate spelling and punctuation. (This requirement must constitute 20% of the marks for each specification as a whole.)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Marking bands for 16-mark AO6: Level 4 (13–16) = sentence demarcation consistently secure and accurate; wide range of punctuation used accurately; uses full range of sentence forms for effect; consistently uses Standard English with secure control of complex grammatical structures; high level of accuracy in spelling including ambitious vocabulary. Level 3 (9–12) = mostly accurate; range of punctuation mostly successful; variety of sentence forms; mostly correct Standard English and generally accurate spelling. Level 2 (5–8) = sometimes accurate; some control of punctuation and sentence forms; some use of Standard English; some accurate spelling of complex words. Level 1 (1–4) = occasional sentence demarcation and punctuation; simple sentence forms; basic accurate spelling. Level 0 = spelling/punctuation so poor meaning is prevented.
